question: What is a non-infectious disease (非傳染病)?
options: A disease transmitted by mosquito bites
A disease that is not caused by pathogens and cannot be spread from person to person, often resulting from genetic, physiological, environmental, or lifestyle factors
A bacterial infection cured by antibiotics
A viral illness spread through respiratory droplets

question: What causes coronary heart disease (CHD / 冠心病)?
options: Viral infection of the pulmonary vein
Build-up of fatty plaques (cholesterol and lipids) on the inner walls of the coronary arteries (atherosclerosis), narrowing the lumen and restricting blood flow to heart muscle
Overproduction of red blood cells in the bone marrow
Excessive intake of vitamin C and dietary fibre

question: If a blood clot (thrombus) blocks a narrowed coronary artery, cardiac muscle cells are deprived of oxygen and glucose for respiration and die, causing a heart attack (myocardial infarction).
options: True / 正確
False / 錯誤

question: Which combination of lifestyle factors significantly increases the risk of developing coronary heart disease?
options: Regular aerobic exercise and a diet rich in fruits and vegetables
A diet high in saturated fats, cholesterol, and salt, smoking, lack of physical exercise, and chronic stress
Drinking plenty of plain water and getting adequate sleep
Eating whole grains and unsaturated vegetable oils

question: How does cigarette smoking increase the risk of cardiovascular diseases such as stroke and coronary heart disease?
options: Nicotine lowers heart rate and dilates arteries.
Nicotine raises blood pressure and heart rate, while carbon monoxide reduces oxygen transport and damages the inner lining of arteries, promoting plaque and clot formation.
Tar increases haemoglobin levels in red blood cells.
Smoking dissolves cholesterol plaques in the aorta.

question: A stroke (中風) occurs when blood supply to part of the brain is interrupted either by a blocked cerebral artery (ischaemic stroke) or a burst blood vessel in the brain (haemorrhagic stroke).
options: True / 正確
False / 錯誤

question: What is cancer (癌症) at the cellular level?
options: A bacterial infection of the lymph nodes
Uncontrolled mitotic division of abnormal cells caused by mutations in genes regulating the cell cycle, forming a malignant tumour that can invade surrounding tissues
Premature aging and death of red blood cells
Accumulation of glycogen in liver cells

question: How does a malignant tumour (惡性腫瘤) differ from a benign tumour (良性腫瘤)?
options: A benign tumour spreads rapidly through the bloodstream; a malignant tumour stays in one place.
A malignant tumour invades nearby tissues and can spread to distant parts of the body via blood or lymph (metastasis / 轉移), whereas a benign tumour remains localized and enclosed in a capsule.
A benign tumour is caused by bacteria; a malignant tumour is caused by fungi.
Only benign tumours are made of living cells.

question: Carcinogens (致癌物), such as tar in tobacco smoke, ultraviolet (UV) radiation, X-rays, and certain chemicals like asbestos, increase the risk of cancer by causing DNA mutations.
options: True / 正確
False / 錯誤

question: Which virus infection is strongly linked to cervical cancer and can be prevented by vaccination?
options: Influenza virus / 流感病毒
Human papillomavirus (HPV) / 人類乳頭瘤病毒
Dengue virus / 登革熱病毒
Norovirus / 諾如病毒

question: Which type of cancer is strongly associated with chronic Hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection and aflatoxins from mouldy food?
options: Lung cancer / 肺癌
Liver cancer / 肝癌
Skin cancer / 皮膚癌
Colorectal cancer / 大腸癌

question: Regular screening tests (such as mammograms, Pap smears, and faecal occult blood tests) help detect cancers at an early stage when treatment is much more successful.
options: True / 正確
False / 錯誤

question: How does radiotherapy (放射治療) treat localized cancerous tumours?
options: By stimulating antibodies against tumour cells
By directing high-energy ionizing radiation at the tumour to damage the DNA of rapidly dividing cancer cells and kill them
By replacing malignant cells with stem cells
By lowering blood cholesterol levels

question: Why does chemotherapy (化療) often cause temporary side effects such as hair loss and nausea?
options: Chemotherapy drugs only target dead cells.
Chemotherapy drugs circulate throughout the body and affect not only cancer cells but also normal rapidly dividing cells (such as hair follicle cells and gut epithelial cells).
Chemotherapy permanently stops insulin secretion.
Chemotherapy destroys all red blood cells permanently.

question: Obesity (肥胖) is a major risk factor for Type 2 diabetes, hypertension (high blood pressure), coronary heart disease, and osteoarthritis.
options: True / 正確
False / 錯誤

question: How is Body Mass Index (BMI / 身體質量指數) calculated to assess weight status in adults?
options: Height (m) ÷ Body mass (kg)
Body mass (kg) ÷ [Height (m)]²
[Body mass (kg)]² ÷ Height (cm)
Waist circumference (cm) × Body mass (kg)

question: Which dietary habit helps reduce the risk of colorectal cancer (大腸癌)?
options: Eating large amounts of processed and red meats with very little water
Consuming plenty of dietary fibre (from fruits, vegetables, and whole grains) to stimulate peristalsis and speed up the passage of waste through the colon
Avoiding all plant foods
Taking daily doses of antibiotics

question: Alcohol abuse can cause liver cirrhosis (肝硬化), fatty liver, high blood pressure, and impaired nervous system coordination.
options: True / 正確
False / 錯誤

question: How does regular aerobic exercise help prevent cardiovascular disease?
options: It increases saturated fat deposits in arteries.
It strengthens the heart muscle, improves blood circulation, helps maintain a healthy body weight, and lowers resting blood pressure and LDL cholesterol.
It eliminates the need for oxygen during respiration.
It stops the pancreas from producing glucagon.

question: What is hypertension (高血壓), and why is it often called a 'silent killer'?
options: Low blood sugar that causes immediate fainting
Persistently elevated arterial blood pressure that often shows no obvious early symptoms while steadily damaging blood vessel walls and increasing the risk of stroke and heart failure
A bacterial infection of the lungs
Sudden drop in heart rate during sleep

question: Reducing dietary sodium (salt) intake helps prevent and manage high blood pressure by reducing excessive water retention in the bloodstream.
options: True / 正確
False / 錯誤

question: Which preventive measure best protects against skin cancer (melanoma)?
options: Avoiding all dietary fats
Limiting prolonged exposure to strong midday sunlight and applying broad-spectrum sunscreen to block UV radiation
Taking iron supplements daily
Drinking distilled water only

question: What is the role of vaccination in preventing certain non-infectious diseases like liver cancer and cervical cancer?
options: Vaccines directly destroy cancerous tumours after metastasis.
Vaccines prevent chronic infections by oncogenic viruses (Hepatitis B virus and HPV) that otherwise trigger malignant cell transformation over time.
Vaccines replace damaged chromosomes in liver cells.
Vaccines neutralize dietary carcinogens in the stomach.

question: Passive smoking (second-hand smoke) also exposes non-smokers to carcinogens and toxic gases, increasing their risk of lung cancer and heart disease.
options: True / 正確
False / 錯誤

question: Which lifestyle combination represents primary prevention (一級預防) of non-infectious diseases?
options: Undergoing heart bypass surgery after a heart attack
Not smoking, eating a balanced low-fat/high-fibre diet, exercising regularly, and limiting alcohol consumption before disease develops
Taking chemotherapy after tumour metastasis
Using an insulin pump for Type 1 diabetes
